docs.title: 🎁 Horror Toy Factory
docs.text: Explore four haunted factory areas in Lutie, uncover the workers' memories and defeat Celine Kimi and her phantom. Complete the run with ten shared treasure chests and spend Bloody Coins at Mister Cat.

docs.title: Quick facts
docs.text: Requirement Vestige Rift rule Entry NPC Catherine Jet Johnson, xmas 237,303 Party 3 or more members, each using a different account Minimum Base Level 90 for every member Readiness Every starting member types !ready in public chat within 60 seconds Time limit 1 hour, starting after everyone confirms readiness Weekly allowance 1 HTF run per account, shared by its characters and separate from Tower and Cellar Weekly reset Monday at 06:00 Philippines time (UTC+8)

docs.title: Getting there
docs.text:
NPC Location Service Catherine Jet Johnson /navi xmas 237/303 Start HTF, rejoin the current area or view weekly run information Mister Cat /navi xmas 240/300 Exchange Bloody Coins for equipment, costumes and supplies
  1. Gather the entire party in Lutie. Everyone must be online, alive and Base Level 90+, with other dialogs, shops and storage closed.
  2. The leader selects Start Horror Toy Factory at Catherine.
  3. Every starting member types !ready in public chat within 60 seconds, keeping the same party roster.
  4. Once everyone is ready, the party enters the first factory area and each account consumes its weekly HTF run.

An expired or unsuccessful readiness check returns the party to its save points without consuming a run. A member who disconnects or leaves Lutie during readiness must return and confirm again.

Use @instanceinfo, or Catherine's Weekly run information, to see the separate HTF, Tower and Cellar allowances. A party can have one of these instances or readiness checks active at a time.

docs.title: Instance rules
docs.text: Feature Rule Progression Complete the four areas in order, then enter the treasure room. Death Normal death rules apply. Players can be resurrected or leave and re-enter. Re-entry Only the original starting characters can rejoin, while at least one original member remains inside. Return through Catherine to the current area. Everyone leaves The instance closes when all original members leave or disconnect. The weekly run remains consumed. Storage Personal and Guild Storage are unavailable inside. Mail RODEX is available inside. Drops Monsters use the configured server drop rates. Bubble Gum does not increase HTF drops. Chests Each of the ten shared party chests opens once and places its rewards on the ground. Chest chances are fixed. Completion Use the final exit portal after the boss and treasure room to record completion. Time limit The original one-hour timer covers encounters and treasure collection.

docs.title: Area 1 - Production line
docs.text:
Speak to a Uniform Box to become a Red Cookie for three minutes. Refresh the disguise before it expires. Exploring without the required disguise can attract Nightmare Cruiser guards, which give no EXP or loot.

Defeat 38 of the production line's 67 monsters. The line then clears and its remaining monsters disappear. Visit the Coordinator in the northwest while disguised, use the nearby Packaged Present to become a Myst Case, then enter the east portal.

Monster Starting count Vicious CookieID: 2989 31 Evil Dwelling BoxID: 2991 36

docs.title: Area 2 - Workers' memories
docs.text:
Renew your Red Cookie disguise at the Uniform Box near Catherine. Speak to all ten workers, each with a three-second listening period. You remain vulnerable to nearby monsters while hearing their memories.

Once all ten workers have spoken, the remaining area monsters disappear. Return to the entrance portal to continue north. Before completing the objective, that portal returns you to the first area.

docs.title: Final area - Celine Kimi
docs.text:
Speak to Celine Kimi and choose to face her and the phantom. Defeat both to open the southwest treasure-room portal.

Enemy Count Role Celine KimiID: 2996 1 MVP Kimi's PhantomID: 2997 1 Companion boss Mechanic Behavior Keep them together Separating Kimi and the phantom by more than 7 cells lets both recover 25% of maximum HP per second, up to full HP. Balance the damage If their HP differs by more than 1.5% of Kimi's maximum HP, the lower-HP boss heals for eight times the difference, capped at maximum HP. Fight inside the room Pulling Kimi outside her fighting area resets the encounter. Speak to her to begin again. Boss abilities Both use Dispell, Critical Wounds, Darkness Attack and Soul Strike. Kimi also uses Power Up below 40% HP.

Celine Kimi is the MVP. Antonio is the Area 3 boss; the phantom is Kimi's companion boss. Nightmare Cruisers and the phantom give no EXP or loot.

Before server rates, ordinary factory monsters give 3,500 Base / 2,200 Job EXP, Antonio gives 18,000 / 10,000, and Kimi gives 400,000 / 220,000, plus 50,000 MVP bonus EXP.

docs.title: 🕥 Hourly rewards
docs.text:
Updated: November 17, 2026.

Earn points while you play, convert them into Gold Coins, and spend the coins on costumes at the Gold Point Manager.

docs.title: Earning points
docs.text:
Setting Value Reward rate 10 points per hour online Progress Shared across characters on the same account Partial hours Saved through logout and server restarts Normal AFK time Counts while the character remains online Offline vending / autotrade Does not earn points Point balance limit 300 points

Earning pauses at the 300-point balance limit. Spend points to make room and resume earning. Changing characters does not create a separate balance or reset accumulated partial-hour progress.

docs.title: Convert points into Gold Coins
docs.text:
Click the hourly timer in the top-right corner to automatically convert every complete bundle of 120 points into one Gold Coin (#7929). Remaining points and partial-hour progress are kept.

Points before clicking Gold Coins received Points left 120 1 0 190 1 70 240 2 0 300 2 60

One coin requires 12 hours at the normal reward rate. Clicking with fewer than 120 points leaves the balance intact.

The coins go into the inventory of the character that clicks the timer. If that character lacks the required inventory capacity or weight allowance, points are retained; make room and click again.

Choose the character that will spend the coins

Points are account-wide, but converted Gold Coins stay with the receiving character. Each coin weighs 1. Coins cannot be dropped, traded, sold to NPCs, mailed, auctioned, placed in a cart, or put in personal or guild storage.

docs.title: Spend your coins
docs.text:
Visit the Gold Point Manager at /navi prt_in 38/104, inside the Coin Exchange building. Enter at Prontera 133,183, beneath the Coin Exchange bubble.

Click the NPC to open the costume exchange shop. Select the costume, add it to the exchange tray, and confirm the purchase using Gold Coins in your inventory. Your character stays in place while the shop is open; close the shop to walk normally again.

Use the timer to convert points and the NPC to shop. There is no separate point-exchange dialogue to work through.

docs.title: 🎯 Kill Count
docs.text:
Updated: November 16, 2026.

Use @kc or @killcount to review a monster's kill history and choose whether to show a private counter above your character. Only one monster type can be actively tracked at a time. Your recorded statistics continue to update even when the overhead counter is Off.

docs.title: Start tracking your last kill
docs.text:
1. Kill the monster you want to track.
  2. Type @kc. When nothing is being tracked, the menu detects the most recent monster credited to you during this login.
  3. Review its summary, then choose Start tracking kills.
  4. Kill more of that monster to see your tracked count above your character.

    5. Opening the menu or pressing Cancel does not start tracking. The confirmation appears privately above your character:

    You started tracking Hill Wind kills.

    Each subsequent credited kill shows:

    Hill Wind kills: 6,409

    The message has no character-name prefix and is visible only to you. There is no five-monster list or capacity indicator.

docs.title: Read the summary
docs.text:
Field Meaning Total kills Your character's recorded credited kills of this monster. Kills without card Credited kills since this monster most recently generated a card. The card-generating kill resets this streak to zero. Cards dropped Cards generated by this monster on kills credited to you, including cards left on the ground or shared with another player. Tracked kills Kills recorded by the active overhead counter since you started or reset it during this login. Shown while tracking is active.

The numbers are grouped with commas. Card pickup, autoloot and pet delivery do not count a generated card a second time. Trades, storage withdrawals and NPC rewards do not add monster-card drops.

Existing total-kill records are retained. Older per-monster card-drop history was not recorded, so Cards dropped and Kills without card begin from the available history under this system; missing historical drops are not reconstructed.

docs.title: Stop, reset or change the monster
docs.text:
Run @kc again while tracking to open the active monster's summary, even if you have since killed something else.

Choice Result Stop tracking kills Turn off the overhead counter and clear its tracked count. Reset track kills for Reset only the tracked count to zero and keep tracking. Cancel Keep the current selection and count.

Neither Stop nor Reset changes Total kills, Cards dropped or Kills without card.

To propose a different monster, use @kc <monster ID>, for example @kc 1002 for Poring. Review the summary and choose Start to replace the active monster. Cancelling keeps your previous selection. @killcount <monster ID> works the same way.

docs.title: Persistence and kill credit
docs.text:
• The confirmed monster selection and recorded statistics are saved per character.
  • The tracked overhead count starts at zero and restarts when you log in again. Earlier kills are not added retroactively.
  • Death and map changes do not reset the tracked count.
  • Kills by your pet, homunculus, mercenary or elemental credit you as their owner.
  • Being in the party alone does not grant a credited kill. No-reward scripted removals and summon timeouts do not count as hunting kills.

docs.title: Card drops versus card receipts
docs.text:
Kill Count records a card when the monster generates it. Card Drop Announcements instead credit the character who successfully receives it. These can be different players after party sharing or a manual pickup.

For example, a card left on the ground increases the killing owner's Cards dropped total, but it does not produce a receipt announcement until somebody collects it.

docs.title: Mercy progress
docs.text: Eligible monster summaries also show Mercy progress: current / 5,000. After 5,000 eligible normal-monster kills without a card, one card is guaranteed. Mercy is automatic and saved separately from the visible tracker; Stop and Reset do not change it. MVPs and mini-bosses are excluded. See Mercy System for eligibility, resets and delivery rules.

docs.title: 🛡️ Kill Steal Protection
docs.text:
Updated: November 10, 2026.

@noks protects ordinary monsters you are fighting from other players' attacks. Choose who may help through its menu, or open @settings > Kill Steal Protection. Both entry points use the same saved choice.

Protection defaults to Party for existing and new characters without a saved choice. Your mode is saved per character and restored on login. A saved Off choice remains Off.

docs.title: Choose a mode
docs.text:
Mode Who may attack your protected monsters? Self You and your own companions only. Party and guild membership do not grant access. Party You and your current party members. Guild You and your current guild members. Party membership alone does not grant access. Disable protection No kill-steal protection for your monsters.

Party and Guild require a matching, nonempty membership. Choosing a mode does not reset a monster's existing protection timers.

docs.title: When protection starts
docs.text:
An eligible monster can become protected when:

  • It selects you or one of your companions as its combat target.
  • You or your companion deal positive damage from outside the monster's aggro range, before its targeting catches up.

Merely selecting a passive monster or starting a targeted cast does not claim it. An already-idle player does not gain a fresh protection window just because a monster targets them.

There is no limit on the number of protected monsters. Your pet, homunculus, mercenary and elemental follow your ownership and access rules.

docs.title: Release timers
docs.text:
Protection ends when any applicable deadline is reached:

Rule Duration When it starts Idle release 5 seconds Since the owner's last attack, skill use or movement. Continuous walking counts as movement. Contest timer 15 seconds At the first unauthorized attack or targeted-cast attempt against the protected monster. Hard cap 30 seconds When that monster first becomes protected.

Chat, item use and emotes do not keep the idle timer alive. Attacking, helping allies or repeatedly attempting to steal a monster does not restart the contest timer or extend the hard cap.

For example, if protection starts at 0 seconds and an outsider first tries to attack at 20 seconds, the 30-second hard cap ends the lock before the contest timer would finish at 35 seconds. Idle release can end it earlier.

Once released, the same ongoing encounter stays open. Continuing to attack does not immediately renew its protection; the monster must drop that target or select a different owner before a new encounter can be protected. Owner death, logout, leaving the map or disabling protection also releases the lock. A respawn starts with fresh state.

docs.title: Check your party
docs.text:
Type @nokscheck to see your own mode and your party members' current modes. The report is private and does not change anyone's settings.

Use Party when everyone in the party should be able to help attack each other's protected monsters. Self can block party members; Guild permits only matching guild members.

Offline members and members whose settings are unavailable on another map server are marked not checked, rather than being reported as Off. Without a party, the command reports your own mode and explains that you are not in a party.

docs.title: Exceptions and normal reward rules
docs.text:
Protection does not apply to:

  • MVPs and Boss-mode mini-bosses.
  • Monsters controlled as native summoned slaves.
  • Towns, PvP, GvG/WoE and Battleground maps.
  • Maps explicitly configured to allow kill stealing.

Attack permission does not replace the normal EXP, loot ownership or party-sharing rules. Use Kill Count to review credited kills and Card Drop Announcements to understand who is credited with receiving a card.

docs.title: 🍀 Mercy System
docs.text: After 5,000 eligible kills of the same normal monster without its card dropping, the Mercy System guarantees one card. Progress is automatic: you do not need to enable it or start a tracked counter.

docs.title: Progress and resets
docs.text:
• Progress is saved per character and monster ID, including across logins.
  • Any natural or guaranteed card drop resets that monster's Mercy streak to zero.
  • The card counts when it drops, even if it stays on the ground or party sharing delivers it to another player.
  • Buying, trading or receiving a card as a quest reward does not reset Mercy.
  • Existing recorded cardless streaks count toward the guarantee. Missing history starts at zero.

The normal card roll happens first. If the threshold kill naturally drops the card, Mercy does not add a second copy. A character whose recorded streak was already 5,000 or higher receives one guarantee on the next eligible kill, rather than retroactive batches of cards.

docs.title: Eligible monsters
docs.text:
Mercy applies only to normal monsters with an available card in their regular drop table.

MVPs and mini-bosses are excluded, including mini-bosses such as Vocal and Bloody Knight. Player-created summons, minions, clones, guardians and deaths that cannot award ordinary loot do not advance Mercy.

Kills credited to you through qualifying pets, homunculi, mercenaries or elementals follow the normal ownership rules. Different monster IDs have separate progress, even when their names are similar.

docs.title: Check your progress
docs.text:
Use @kc or @killcount to view Mercy progress: current / 5,000 in an eligible monster's summary. Ineligible monsters are marked accordingly.

Starting, stopping or resetting the visible Kill Count tracker does not change your Mercy streak.

docs.title: Collecting the card
docs.text:
A guaranteed card follows normal loot ownership, party sharing, inventory-capacity and Autoloot rules. If it falls to the ground, collect it normally or with Area Loot. A personal message tells the credited killer when Mercy guarantees a card.

Mercy does not permanently raise card drop rates. Card Drop Announcements still occur when somebody successfully receives the card.

docs.title: 🌱 Novice Training Grounds
docs.text:
Updated: November 18, 2026.

Every newly created character starts as a Novice in the training grounds. Learn the controls, practice combat and explore the first classes before graduating with Job Level 10, starter equipment, supplies and 10,000z.

Starting your adventure

New characters arrive at new_zone01 53,111, beside Sprakki. Existing characters keep their current locations and progress. Graduation rewards are available once per character.

docs.title: Your training route
docs.text:
1. Meet Sprakki at new_zone01 53,114. Learn movement, camera controls and useful shortcuts, then cross the bridge and enter the building at 148,112.
  2. Learn equipment and items with Brade at new_zone02 100,105. Keep your starting Knife and Cotton Shirt equipped and answer the lesson question. Brade gives you 10 Novice Potions for practice.
  3. Learn skills with Jinha at new_zone02 115,120. Answer his skill-point question and learn First Aid, then enter the hunting grounds through 73,106.
  4. Defeat five Porings, then report to Brade at new_zone03 96,30. Use Alt+U to follow your quest progress.
  5. Complete at least one class lesson with a guide listed below. Each lesson includes a short three-monster hunt. Return to the same guide to finish it.
  6. Ask combat Brade to proceed to graduation, then speak to Hanson at new_zone04 100,24. Confirm graduation to receive your package and enter Main Office.

Training progress is saved when you log out. Combat Brade offers free HP/SP recovery while you are training. If you die, you return to your current training checkpoint.

docs.title: Training-ground rules
docs.text:
The grounds are for learning, with EXP and quest kill progress enabled. Monsters here do not drop normal loot, cards or Vestige Coins. Teleportation, return items and monster-summoning branches are disabled; follow the tutorial's doors and NPCs to advance.

Once a character graduates, the training grounds cannot be used to claim another starter package.

docs.title: 🎛️ Personal settings
docs.text:
Updated: November 16, 2026.

Type @settings to choose how pets, songs, messages and other information appear on your screen. Preferences are saved automatically and restored when you log in. Configure visual, sound and chat preferences through this menu.

Most preferences are shared across your account, including channel visibility. Your storage withdrawal weight limit, Area Loot toggle, autoloot configuration, Restock groups, Quick Store groups and Kill Steal Protection mode are saved per character.

docs.title: Default chat channels
docs.text:
Every existing and new player automatically joins these channels when entering the game:

Channel Use Message color #main General discussion Orange #recruit Party and guild recruitment Blue #market Buying and selling Red

To send a message, enter the channel name in the whisper recipient box, then type your message. For example, set the recipient to #recruit to look for a party.

Open @settings > Channel Config to turn a channel On or Off for your account. A saved Off choice is respected on later logins; automatic joining does not reset it. These preferences affect your own view, not other players.

Turning a channel On joins it, subject to normal channel access. #map and the guild-alliance channel retain their existing map/guild behavior.

docs.title: Pets and song music
docs.text:
Open @settings and select the relevant option:

Setting Menu choice or effect Hide Pets Choose Show all pets, Only show my pet, Only show other pets, or Hide all pets. Show all is the default. Mute Pets Turn pet talk and emotes On or Off for your view. Pets still function normally. Mute Songs Turn song muting On or Off. Musical notes, ground effects and other sound effects remain available.

Hidden pets do not chatter on your screen. Visible pets remain audible unless you also enable Mute Pets. Mute Pets and Mute Songs are Off by default.

Mute Pets and Hide Pets also apply to @pettalk speech and pet emotes. These preferences affect only your view; homunculus speech and player chat remain visible. Companion speech is still logged under its owner. See Homunculus and Pet Commands for usage and chat rules.

A song already playing may finish after you change its setting. The setting filters subsequent song playback; stop the current performance and cast again to check it. Turning Mute Songs Off restores song audio.

docs.title: Show Rare Drops
docs.text:
Select Show Rare Drops in the menu and enter a threshold from 1 to 100%. This sets the maximum original database drop chance for a personal loot notice. For example, 1% reports successful monster drops with a base chance of 1% or less.

Server rates, weekend rates and personal drop bonuses do not change which base chance is compared. This option reports items you actually receive; it does not change drop rates. Enter 0 in the menu to disable these notices. They are Off by default.

docs.title: Card Drop Illustration
docs.text:
Card Drop Illustration is On by default. When you receive a supported monster card through the tracked loot system, its artwork appears at the bottom right for five seconds, for you only. Select Card Drop Illustration in the settings menu to turn it On or Off.

Card Drop Announcements name the successful recipient and show their recorded copy number for that specific card. The monster kill count is included for the recipient's own credited kill; party-shared cards and pickups from somebody else's kill omit it. Announcements follow Public chat filtering and the account's Announcement Config > Drop choice. Received copies are separate from the generated-card statistics in Kill Count.

Ordinary trades, NPC rewards and storage withdrawals do not trigger monster-drop artwork. Artwork is skipped when an NPC dialog is active or an illustration is unavailable. A later NPC illustration takes precedence over the timed card image.

See Card exchange for exchanging unwanted cards; exchange points are separate from these display preferences.

docs.title: Information and visibility
docs.text:
Choose these options in @settings:

Setting Behavior Default Show Experience Turn gained-EXP messages On or Off. On Show Guildmates HP Show nearby guildmates' HP bars. Turning it Off retains party and Battleground HP bars. On Previous Teleport Position Mark your departure cell on the minimap after a teleport within the same map. Cross-map travel does not create this marker. Off Direct Message Warning Play a sound and show a personal on-screen notice for an accepted whisper. Alerts are limited to one per two seconds; server notices and channel messages do not trigger them. Off Time Mode Choose Server cycle, Always day or Always night. Only your view changes. Server cycle Hide Headgear and Costumes during WoE Hide everyone's headgear, costume headgear and robe visuals, including your own, on castle maps during their active WoE session. Equipment and bonuses remain intact. Off Status Color Effect Choose Show status aura or Hide status aura. Show

Existing saved choices take precedence over defaults.

docs.title: Announcement configuration
docs.text:
Choose individual categories under @settings > Announcement Config:

  • Welcome
  • Drop
  • Battlegrounds
  • Kill
  • Community News
  • MVP
  • Event
  • PvP Arena

Select a category to turn its announcements On or Off for your account. All categories are visible by default. These choices control existing announcements; they do not activate an otherwise unavailable event or announcement system. General announcements use Event, while rotating EXP-region notices use Community News.

Card Drop Announcements use Drop and are filtered as Public chat. Card Drop Illustration remains an independent option.

The High-contrast yellow option in the same submenu recolors server announcements for easier reading. It is Off by default.

docs.title: Kill Steal Protection
docs.text:
Open Kill Steal Protection inside @settings to choose Self, Party, Guild or Disable protection. @noks opens the same menu. The default is Party, and the choice is saved per character, including a saved Off choice.

Use @nokscheck to review party members' current modes without changing them. Offline or otherwise unavailable members are marked not checked.

Locks release after 5 seconds without owner attacks, skill use or movement, 15 seconds after the first unauthorized attempt, or 30 seconds from acquisition, whichever applies first. Chat does not refresh activity. See Kill Steal Protection for acquisition rules, mode permissions and map/boss exclusions.

docs.title: Storage weight limit and restock
docs.text:
Select Storage Withdrawal Weight Limit in @settings and enter a value from 1 to 100%. This chooses the maximum carried-weight percentage after a withdrawal from personal storage. The default is 100%, saved separately for each character. This does not increase carrying capacity or change overweight recovery restrictions.

Restock now uses named item/quantity lists. Open Restock Supplies to configure target inventory totals, or Quick Store to choose item IDs whose entire eligible inventory quantities should be deposited. Each feature supports 40 groups of 40 items, with one active group per type.

Transfers require already-open Main Storage in a town, including Midgard Expedition Camp, Manuk and Splendide. Restock stays strictly below 90% carried weight and respects a lower personal withdrawal limit. Quick Store can unload items while overweight and never asks for a quantity.

See Fast storage for full setup, item eligibility and the Jellopy #909 example. The dedicated @restockconfig / @qstoreconfig menus open the same saved configuration; @restock / @qstore run the active lists.

docs.title: Autoloot configuration
docs.text:
Choose Autoloot inside @settings, or use @lootconfig to open the same menu. Configure Main Autoloot's original-drop-chance threshold, an ignore list of 100 items, and up to 40 custom groups of 100 items. Changes apply immediately and persist per character.

An active group adds its items even when they are ignored or Main Autoloot is Off. To loot everything except Jellopy, enable Main Autoloot at 100%, ignore #909, and ensure the active group does not include #909.

See Advanced autoloot for filter precedence, defaults and setup. Visual/chat preferences remain configured only through @settings.

See bulk purchases and storage for the separate large-purchase feature.

docs.title: Area Loot
docs.text: Choose Area Loot (3x3) inside @settings to toggle nearby manual pickup. It is Off by default, saved per character, and synchronized with @arealoot. A successful clicked pickup also collects eligible items in the 3x3 square centered on that item. See Area Loot for ownership, carrying-capacity and no-chaining rules.

Bonuses apply while the pet is active and at the stated intimacy. Each row is the complete bonus at that tier, not an amount added to the rows above. Equipment is not required for the listed owner bonuses.

docs.title: Artwork
docs.text: Pet artwork is stored with this site rather than hotlinked, and item icons match the installed game data. Ragnarok Online artwork belongs to Gravity. Gameplay values and recipes above come from Vestige Rift's active server definitions.

docs.title: 🐱 Pet System
docs.text:
Tame a companion, build its trust and evolve it into a new form. The illustrated pet catalogue lists 115 pet entries, their owner bonuses, food, accessories and 43 evolution paths. Every evolution ingredient has a picture and an exact quantity.

Browse pets and evolution recipes

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
1. Obtain the taming item listed for your chosen pet and use it on a matching, living monster.
  2. Hatch its egg with a Pet Incubator.
  3. Carry the pet's correct food and feed it while hungry. For eligible pets, enable Automatic feeding in the pet window (Alt+J).
  4. Reach Loyal intimacy, remove the pet accessory and collect the listed ingredients before evolving.

Pet Incubator (#643) is used to hatch or switch pets. Pet food and Incubators are sold by the Pet Dealers.

docs.title: Taming
docs.text:
Each catalogue entry identifies the taming item and the server's configured base capture chance. A lure is consumed only after a valid target is accepted; a genuine failed capture consumes one. Cancelled selections, dead targets and mismatched targets do not consume it.

For ordinary taming, the base capture chance doubles only when the monster is strictly below 1% HP. At exactly 1% HP it remains unchanged.

Taming Gift Set (#12105) draws from 55 registered taming lures. It supplies lures, not guaranteed pets.

Abracadabra uses the pet's configured capture rules. Evolved forms with an explicit Abracadabra setting use a fixed 0.01% capture chance. The bonusless cosmetic Bacsojin and the evolved bonus-bearing Bacsojin are separate pets; check which egg you are buying.

docs.title: Feeding and intimacy
docs.text:
Hunger decreases by 3 points every 60 seconds while a pet is active. Auto-feed triggers at 25 hunger or below, requires the correct food in your inventory and must be switched on for that pet. The catalogue shows which pets support it.

Relationship Intimacy Awkward 1-99 Shy 100-249 Neutral 250-749 Cordial 750-899 Loyal 900-1,000

New and newly evolved pets start at 250 intimacy (Neutral). Intimacy is capped at 1,000 and never drops below 1. Owner death costs 5 intimacy.

The catalogue's feeding gain is the amount awarded at 11-25 hunger:

Pet group Intimacy per properly timed feeding First evolution tier +40 Other ordinary and final forms +30 Incubus, Succubus and Phreeoni +20

Feeding at 26-75 hunger gives 75% of that gain, rounded down; feeding at 0-10 gives half. Feeding above 75 can reduce intimacy. Keep the correct food available rather than overfeeding to rush Loyal.

If a pet starves, it returns to its egg at 1 intimacy. It retains its identity and nickname instead of disappearing permanently.

docs.title: Switching pets
docs.text:
Use a Pet Incubator while a pet is active, then choose another valid egg. Keep one inventory slot free. A successful switch returns the current pet to its egg and consumes one Incubator.

Cancelling the egg-selection window leaves the active pet and Incubator unchanged. Invalid selections do not consume the item.

docs.title: Evolution
docs.text:
1. Raise the active pet to Loyal (900+).
  2. Remove its accessory and carry all ingredients listed under Evolves into in the catalogue.
  3. Open the pet window, select the evolution option, choose the target form and confirm.
  4. Use an Incubator to hatch the resulting egg.

The ingredients are checked before withdrawal. Refined, carded or equipped gear is not taken as ordinary recipe equipment. A rejected recipe consumes no materials.

After evolution:

  • The original egg becomes the evolved pet's egg in the same slot. Evolution does not award a second copy of the old pet.
  • The pet keeps its identity and any custom nickname.
  • Intimacy resets to 250, and hunger resets to 100.
  • Auto-feed stays enabled if it was on and the new form supports it. Otherwise, enable it when the form becomes eligible.

docs.title: Example: Poring to Mastering
docs.text:
Material Quantity Yggdrasil Leaf (#610) 10 Unripe Apple (#619) 3

A Loyal Poring with no accessory evolves into Mastering. Hatch the Mastering Egg afterward. See Poring and Mastering for their bonuses and next steps.

docs.title: Classic-compatible ingredients
docs.text:
The recipes use obtainable server materials in place of three ingredients from later content:

Original ingredient Vestige Rift requirement Eggring Card 1 Drops Card (#4004) 500 Sweets Coins 500 Vestige Coins (#7539) 2 Memory of Gyol 200 Skel-Bones (#932)

All quantities in the catalogue already include these substitutions.

docs.title: Fixed-chance egg drops
docs.text:
These are final drop chances. Server rates, weekend rates, Bubble Gum and LUK do not multiply them. Other monster drops keep their usual rules.

Monster Pet egg Chance Dracula Familiar 0.45% Galion Roween 0.03% Phreeoni Phreeoni 0.09% Dark Illusion Dark Priest 0.09% Dark Lord Dark Priest 0.90% Valkyrie Randgris Valkyrie Randgris 0.15%

A dropped egg contains a real pet. If inventory cannot accept it, delivery uses an owner-protected ground egg.

docs.title: Bonuses and visibility
docs.text:
Each pet's owner bonus is listed by intimacy in the catalogue. These are complete tier totals, so do not add several rows together. Some pets provide no owner stat bonus.

Incubus keeps Vestige Rift's existing Loyal bonus: +3% Max SP, plus a 5% chance to recover 5% of physical weapon damage as SP.

Blue Moon Loli Ruri has a 5% chance per incoming physical hit to cast Kyrie Eleison at the eligible intimacy tiers. It casts Level 2, or your learned level if higher.

Use Personal Settings for Hide Pets and Mute Pets. Visual and chatter preferences do not remove the pet's owner bonuses.

docs.title: 🦋 Quality of life
docs.text: Updated: November 20, 2026.

docs.title: Visual AFK Status
docs.text:
An AFK sign appears above your character after 60 seconds idle on eligible hunting maps, temporarily replacing the upper-headgear appearance. Walking, attacking, skill use, item use or equipping an item clears it immediately. Equipment bonuses are preserved.

Towns and town interiors, autotrade, open vending/buying shops and WoE castle maps are excluded. See Visual AFK Status.

docs.title: Personal settings and chat channels
docs.text:
Use @settings to save account-wide preferences for pets, song music, drop notices, card artwork, EXP messages, guild HP, teleport markers, whisper alerts, day/night, announcements and WoE visuals. Storage withdrawal limits, autoloot preferences, Restock groups and Quick Store groups are saved per character.

#main, #recruit and #market are automatically joined by existing and new players. Saved channel Off choices remain respected. Use Channel Config to manage them.

See Personal settings for menu options and defaults. The farming and storage tools below use the same @settings menu and also have their dedicated entry points.

docs.title: Advanced autoloot
docs.text:
Use @settings > Autoloot or @lootconfig to manage Main Autoloot, its 100-item ignore list, and 40 custom groups of 100 items. All preferences save per character. Main Autoloot compares original database drop chances; one active group adds selected item IDs even when ignored or Main Autoloot is Off.

For example, enable Main Autoloot at 100%, ignore Jellopy #909, and keep it out of the active group to leave it on the ground. Manual pickup remains available. See Advanced autoloot for setup and restrictions.

docs.title: Restock and Quick Store
docs.text:
Each tool supports 40 per-character groups with 40 items per group. Configure them through @settings > Restock Supplies / Quick Store, or their dedicated configuration menus.

  • @restock withdraws available supplies up to target inventory quantities, strictly below 90% weight and respecting any lower personal limit.
  • @qstore deposits all eligible inventory units of listed item IDs. Add Jellopy #909 to store all eligible Jellopy; no quantity or Keep field is configured.

Both require Main Storage already open in a town, including Midgard Expedition Camp, Manuk and Splendide. Normal capacity and item restrictions remain. See Fast storage for instructions.

docs.title: Build Manager
docs.text:
Save ten stat builds and ten separate skill builds per character at the Build Manager, Main Office 118,32, near Reset Girl at 118,28. Saving, overwriting, renaming and deleting are free; loading either build type costs 5,000z.

Builds persist after relogging. A class change deletes saved skill builds. Stat builds hide below their saved Base Level and reappear when that level is reached again. Point budgets, caps and skill prerequisites are checked before payment; permanent platinum skills remain learned.

See Build Manager for instructions, reset effects and restrictions.

docs.title: Increased sitting recovery
docs.text:
After seven seconds without attacking or taking damage, a sitting character recovers 3% of Max HP and Max SP every 1.5 seconds. An empty bar takes approximately 51 seconds of eligible pulses to fill, plus the initial combat delay. Standing retains ordinary recovery.

Eligible percentage pulses replace ordinary natural/skill sitting ticks rather than stacking with them. Fractional recovery carries between pulses. Attacks, including misses, offensive damaging skills and received damage restart the combat delay; paying a skill's normal resource cost alone does not.

Overweight disables the increase. Normal recovery restrictions are respected separately for HP and SP, including death, hidden states, disabling statuses and blocked recovery resources. Asura Strike blocks the increased recovery for five minutes during the session; actual relogging clears that session penalty and the native SP penalty as described in class changes.

Super Novice Doridori doubles normal recovery, not these percentage pulses.

docs.title: RODEX mail
docs.text:
Attendance rewards arrive through RODEX after you claim them in Attendance Check. Logging in or opening the attendance window alone does not send a reward. Attendance claims are limited to one per account per Philippine calendar day.

Mail can be used from ordinary towns and fields under the normal map and access restrictions.

Attached item stacks Postage 1 2,500z 2 5,000z 3 7,500z 4 10,000z 5 10,000z
  • Maximum five attached stacks and 2,000 total item weight.
  • Items must pass both trade and mail restrictions. Bound and rental items cannot be attached.
  • Native inventory capacity, receiving-weight checks, 2% attached-Zeny tax and daily 100-mail limit remain.
  • Mail expires 14 days after sending, including unclaimed items and Zeny. There is no extra return-to-sender window.
  • Receiving has no new postage charge.

During WoE, mail is blocked only inside castles whose relevant WoE session is active. Ordinary maps remain usable. FE and SE castles follow their respective sessions; custom castles without a registered siege type follow either active session. Castle mail is available outside its active siege. An already-open mailbox does not bypass the restriction.

docs.title: Party buff letters
docs.text:
Active buffs appear before online party members' names, in this fixed order:

Marker Buff B Blessing A Increase AGI F Full Chemical Protection coverage S Soul Link U Assumptio + Devotion on the protected recipient

Example: [BAFSU+] Infinite.

Updates are triggered by buff application, expiry/removal and relevant equipment changes, without waiting for the fallback party timer. Ordinary network/client latency still applies.

F requires chemical-protection coverage for all currently equipped applicable slots. A two-handed weapon user does not need a shield coating. Equivalent individual coatings also count; partial coverage does not show F.

These labels do not rename the character. Long names may be shortened in the bounded party-menu field; use the full character name if a shortened label is ambiguous.

docs.title: Bulk purchases and personal storage
docs.text:
Buying exactly 30,000 units of one stackable item at a standard Zeny NPC shop opens a confirmation. Confirming sends the items directly to account Main Storage, using the normal price and Merchant discount. Carried inventory weight does not block that direct-storage purchase.

This covers ordinary SHOP NPCs and standard Zeny traders, including the tool dealers and Gunslinger Supplies. Player vending and special-currency, barter, market and attached custom purchase handlers retain their original rules. A bulk order must contain only one item type; smaller purchases still go to inventory.

Cancelling, closing or timing out the confirmation does not purchase anything. Confirmation rechecks the quote, shop access, price, balance and storage capacity. Failed insertion refunds the payment; a quote cannot be replayed.

Personal storage supports ten stacks per stackable item ID, each up to 30,000 units, for a normal maximum of 300,000 units. Partial compatible stacks fill first. Variants share the ten-stack limit but incompatible variants do not merge. Item-specific smaller stack limits, storage slots and item/bound restrictions still apply. Guild storage retains its normal rules.

docs.title: Sensible teleporting
docs.text: Random Fly Wing and Teleport destinations reject NPC touch areas, active player Warp Portal cells and impassable cells. If no safe destination is found, the teleport fails instead of using an unsafe fallback. Deliberate return/save-point warps retain their normal behavior.

docs.title: Rotating EXP regions
docs.text:
Two regions or dungeon groups, rather than two individual maps, receive independently selected 20-30% Base and Job kill EXP bonuses. They rotate together every 48-72 hours.

Use @bonusmaps to see the active groups, eligible maps, percentages and next rotation in Philippine time. Eligible maps need natural spawns; towns, instances, PvP, castles/WoE, Battlegrounds and maps blocking the applicable EXP are excluded.

The bonus multiplies the active rates:

Base rate With a 20-30% region bonus Weekday 20x 24x-26x Weekend 25x 30x-32.5x

Quest EXP, item/card drops and the separate native MVP bonus award are unaffected. Selections and deadlines persist through normal restarts; overdue selections rotate on startup.

docs.title: Summon timeout
docs.text:
Player item-generated monsters, including Dead Branch and Bloody Branch summons, and eligible Abracadabra Class Change/Monocell transformations have a maximum one-hour lifetime. Minions inherit the original deadline; transformations do not extend it. Shorter native lifetimes still apply.

Timeout removes them with no EXP, loot or kill credit. Normal kills before timeout retain their rewards. Ordinary natural/quest spawns, guardians and protected event-bound monsters retain their normal lifecycle.

docs.title: Rebirth weight allowance
docs.text: Valkyrie permits up to 500 displayed carried weight for rebirth. Existing Zeny, level/class, skill-point, cart, falcon and mount requirements remain.

docs.title: Same-stat food stacking
docs.text:
Foods of the same stat coexist by potency. Only the strongest surviving tier contributes its bonus. Lower-tier timers continue counting down while suppressed; they do not pause. When the strongest expires, the next strongest unexpired tier resumes with its remaining time.

Each newly consumed tier starts at its full scripted duration; consuming the same tier from the same source refreshes it. Normal and cash foods are compared together. Different stats operate independently. Only the effective food icon/countdown is shown. Saved tiers follow native offline-timer and source-specific removal rules.

Example: use +3 STR for 20 minutes, wait two minutes, then use +10 STR for five minutes. After the +10 ends, the +3 resumes for its remaining 13 minutes.

docs.title: Incubus pet
docs.text: At Loyal intimacy (900+), Incubus grants +3% Max SP and a 5% chance to recover 5% of physical weapon damage as SP. SP leech is random and requires missing SP to observe recovery. See the Pet System and illustrated pet catalogue for feeding, auto-feed, intimacy tiers and evolution.

docs.title: Respawn fallback
docs.text: • Returning to the last save point repairs an unavailable/disabled saved map to the configured Prontera fallback, rather than reviving in place due to that invalid map. Valid saved points and Battleground respawns retain their normal rules.

docs.title: Hourly rewards
docs.text:
Earn 10 account-wide points per hour online, up to a 300-point balance. Click the top-right timer to convert complete 120-point bundles into Gold Coins; spend them at the Gold Point Manager in the Coin Exchange building, prt_in 38,104. The costume shop keeps your character stationary until it is closed.

See Hourly rewards for saved partial-hour progress, inventory requirements, coin restrictions and the current sample costume.

docs.title: Convenient dealers
docs.text:
43 existing Tool Dealers now share the 35-item Enhanced Tool catalogue, and 8 existing Pet Groomers share the 48-item Pet catalogue at their original locations. Jackie and Gunslinger Supplies are inside Main Office, at 136,29 and 136,35 respectively.

See Convenient dealers for prices, custom kunai elements, NPC resale values and the complete location directory.

docs.title: Card exchange
docs.text: Putty in Main Office exchanges eligible loose cards for 10 account-wide card points each. The catalogue offers 14 rewards, including manuals, consumables, +10 stat foods, Old Card Album and Bloody Branch for 120 points. Six cards are blacklisted, and favorite, bound, rental and socketed cards are protected.

docs.title: Market Street and offline shops
docs.text:
The vendor system adds an organized market, shop searches, pricing limits and one stackable-item listing per account. Enter through Merchants Warp at prontera 164,174.

Use @ws / @wb for selling/buying search windows, or @ws2 / @wb2 for text results. Remote trading works in towns. @at2 keeps a shop open while returning you to character selection so another character on the same account can play. Use @importshop for the current character's last shop and @vendrecap for its retained sales summary.

See the full vendor guide for allowed maps, permits, account limits and expected first-attempt behavior.

docs.title: Area Loot
docs.text: Turn Area Loot (3x3) On in @settings, or toggle it with @arealoot. A successful manual pickup also collects eligible ground items in the 3x3 square centered on the clicked item. It is Off by default and saved per character. See Area Loot.

docs.title: Mercy System
docs.text: After 5,000 eligible kills of a normal monster without its card dropping, one card is guaranteed. Progress is automatic, persistent per character and monster, and visible through @kc. MVPs and mini-bosses are excluded. See Mercy System.

docs.title: Refining
docs.text: All equipment refiners offer Classic refining with normal ores and bulk targets, or a Visual interface using enriched ores one attempt at a time. Both stop at +10; HD ores are unavailable. See Refining System for costs, success rates and locations.

docs.title: Vestige Coins and Lydia
docs.text: Eligible monsters can drop Vestige Coins, a tradable currency with fixed 5% drops and listed species exceptions. Lydia in the Coin Exchange building, prt_in 38,108 offers 26 rewards. Her Bubble Gum and Putty's are the same +150% for 30 minutes item.

docs.title: 📜 Quest changes
docs.text:
Updated: November 7, 2026.

These quests keep their existing access requirements and story progression, with the changes below.

Quest Original behavior Vestige Rift changes The Sign Failing Part 6A/6B grants EXP and permanently blocks progress until a GM resets it. Failure starts a 15-minute cooldown. Gen returns the Symbol of the Nine Realms so you can retry. Failed attempts no longer grant EXP. Onward to the New World A shared battlefield requires 40 Allied Soldier kills within 15 minutes. Each party gets a private battlefield with 50 kills in 20 minutes. Only the starting leader receives quest credit. The quest log tracks progress, and soldiers respawn immediately. Ore downgrading The Utan Shaman divides up to ten pure elemental stones per visit. Choose one stone or the entire carried stack of the selected stone type.

docs.title: The Sign: retrying a failed ordeal
docs.text:
Failing Part 6A or 6B, including running out of time in the challenge room, starts a 15-minute cooldown. The cooldown continues through logout and server restarts.

  1. Speak to Gen, the Depressing Man in Niflheim: /navi niflheim 146/241.
  2. Wait until the cooldown has finished. Gen tells you how much time remains if you return early.
  3. Make room for the Symbol of the Nine Realms. Gen returns it without creating an extra copy if you already carry one.
  4. Bring the symbol to Kirkena or Serin to restart from the symbol hand-in.

Leftover loan items from the failed attempt are cleared when Gen resets that part of the quest. Successful quest rewards remain unchanged; failed attempts award no EXP.

Previously failed characters

If your character was already stuck in an old failed state, speaking to Gen starts its first 15-minute retry cooldown.

docs.title: Onward to the New World: party battlefield
docs.text: Speak to Munkenro when you reach his combat test: /navi moc_fild22b 230/197.

docs.title: Starting the test
docs.text:
• You must be in a party. A one-person party is allowed.
  • Only the party leader can start the test.
  • Every party member must be online and on the same public staging map when the leader starts.
  • Your party enters its own battlefield, allowing other parties to run their tests independently.

docs.title: Objective and credit
docs.text:
Defeat 50 Allied Soldiers within 20 minutes. Defeated soldiers respawn immediately while the test is active.

The starting leader's quest log shows the kill objective and progress. Party members can help defeat the soldiers, but only the starting leader advances this quest and receives its completion reward. Eligible party kills count across the battlefield while that leader is online, in the instance, and still in the owning party.

docs.title: Leaving, finishing, or retrying
docs.text:
Speak to Munkenro on the public staging map to re-enter an active test after leaving or reconnecting. Re-entry keeps the original deadline and starting leader; it does not reset the timer.

On success, the party returns to the public staging map and the starting leader speaks to Munkenro to claim the normal quest reward. When time runs out, the party returns without completion credit and the leader can start another attempt. A new attempt resets the kill objective.

docs.title: Ore downgrading: one stone or a full stack
docs.text:
Visit the Utan Shaman in Umbala: /navi um_in 44/71. The existing language and shaman-access quest requirements still apply.

Pure stone ID Rough stone received Great Nature 997 Green Live Mystic Frozen 995 Crystal Blue Flame Heart 994 Red Blood Rough Wind 996 Wind of Verdure

Choose the stone type, select one stone or your entire carried stack, and confirm the exchange. The full-stack option uses only that selected stone type from your inventory.

Each pure stone independently produces 6?10 rough stones, retaining the original yield. If the result exceeds your carrying weight, inventory space, or item-stack capacity, your original stones are returned and the exchange does not complete. You can also cancel before confirming.

docs.title: 🔨 Refining System
docs.text: Equipment refiners offer a choice between Classic Refiner and Visual Refiner. Both use our Pre-Renewal refining rules and stop at +10.

docs.title: Choose an interface
docs.text:
Interface Accepted ores Equipment Refining options Classic Refiner Normal ores only Must be equipped One attempt, safe-limit batch or a chosen target level Visual Refiner Enriched ores only May be selected from inventory without equipping One animated attempt, with displayed success chance and material requirements

HD ores are not offered in either interface. Normal ores cannot be used in the Visual Refiner, and enriched ores cannot be used in the Classic Refiner.

Failure destroys the item

An unsuccessful attempt destroys the equipment, including its cards and options. Enriched ores improve success chances but do not protect against destruction.

docs.title: Classic Refiner
docs.text:
Equip an identified, refinable weapon or armor below +10. Rental equipment cannot be refined. Select the equipment, then choose Refine once, Refine to the safe limit, or Choose a target refine level.

A bulk order charges one ore and one fee for each attempt actually made. It stops on failure, insufficient materials, insufficient Zeny or reaching the selected target. Canceling before confirmation consumes nothing.

Select your equipment in the interface, choose its enriched ore and refine one level at a time. Every attempt costs one ore and 2,000z.

These are the same standard items supplied by existing boxes and reward packages. Duplicate ores were converted to these IDs with their quantities preserved, so the interface offers only one ore option for the selected equipment.

docs.text: Updated: November 10, 2026.

docs.title: Core settings
docs.text:
Setting Current value Episode profile 14.2: Eclage, with a strict content allowlist Game mode Classic Pre-Renewal Maximum Base Level 99 Maximum Job Level 70, subject to the class-specific caps below Maximum base stat 99, including baby characters Maximum ASPD 190 Instant-cast DEX threshold 150 under classic cast-time rules Party EXP sharing range 20 levels Minimum skill delay 100 milliseconds; higher skill-specific delays still apply Minimum usable-item interval 50 milliseconds; item-specific restrictions still apply Server time Philippine Standard Time, UTC+08:00 Server language English

Novices retain Job Level 10. First jobs and ordinary non-transcendent second jobs generally retain Job Level 50. Transcendent second jobs, Super Novice/Super Baby and the customized Soul Linker/Baby Soul Linker reach Job Level 70.

docs.text:
Rate Monday-Friday Saturday-Sunday Monster Base EXP 20x 25x Monster Job EXP 20x 25x Normal non-card drops 20x 25x Normal cards 5x 5x MVP and mini-boss non-card drops 3x 3x MVP bonus item rewards 3x 3x MVP and mini-boss cards 1x 1x Quest EXP 5x 5x Pet and homunculus intimacy gain 3x 3x

A standard 0.01% card becomes 0.05% for a normal monster and remains 0.01% for an MVP or mini-boss. Drop probabilities cannot exceed 100%.

Weekend rates run from Saturday 00:00 until Monday 00:00 in Philippine time. Card, boss-drop, quest-EXP and intimacy multipliers remain static. Rotating hunting-region bonuses multiply the active weekday/weekend monster EXP rates; see quality of life.

docs.title: Content profile
docs.text:
The server uses an explicit Episode 14.2 allowlist for maps, monsters, items, quests and regional scripts. Later content is excluded. This is an adapted classic-server profile, not an unmodified official Renewal database. Eclage's original level-100/120 requirements are adapted to level 90; existing level-99 requirements remain.

Some convenience features are explicit exceptions to the episode cutoff, including RODEX, Market Street and the vendor system, Infinite Fly Wing, the documented custom platinum skills, and the selected ammunition, kunai and pet supplies in the dealer catalogue. Their availability does not enable the rest of the later-episode content.

docs.title: Important map definitions
docs.text:
• Natural MVP map: a map with a positive-count natural MVP spawn definition, identified by the monster's native MVP spawn flag or MVP EXP. It remains an MVP map while the MVP is dead. Branch summons alone do not change the classification; ordinary mini-boss maps are not automatically included.
  • GvG/WoE map rules: class restrictions that use the GvG/castle map flags apply on those maps even outside the active siege, where stated in the class guide.
  • RODEX siege restriction: mail is blocked only in a castle during its relevant active WoE session. It is available on ordinary maps during WoE.

See class changes for skill-specific exceptions and quality of life for the mail rules.

docs.title: Trading and exchanges
docs.text:
Shops may open in Market Street, Payon, Morocc, Alberta and Comodo only. Pricing rules and the one-listing-per-stackable-item-ID per account limit apply to selling, buying and offline shops; see the vendor system. Hardware-ID enforcement is deferred.

Card exchange points are shared across the account and are separate from hourly reward points and Gold Coins. Putty offers 14 card-point rewards, including consumables, +10 stat foods, Old Card Album and Bloody Branch.

docs.title: Chat channels and saved preferences
docs.text:
All existing and new players automatically join #main for discussion, #recruit for recruitment and #market for trading. A channel explicitly turned Off in @settings stays Off for that account on later logins.

See Personal settings for channel controls, display preferences and character-specific storage/restock limits.

docs.title: 💰 Vendor system
docs.text:
Updated: November 17, 2026.

Find shops, buy and sell from towns, or keep a merchant trading while you play another character on the same account.

Start here

Enter Market Street through Merchants Warp at /navi prontera 164/174, marked with a Market bubble. Open a shop, then use @at2 to return directly to character selection while the shop stays open.

docs.title: Market Street
docs.text:
Market Street uses map prt_mk, with arrival at 162,142. It has numbered vending spots, a Vending Helper, a Spot Picker and personal-storage access.

NPC / destination Navigation Service Merchants Warp /navi prontera 164/174 Enter Market Street Market center /navi prt_mk 162/142 Arrival and @market destination Vending Helper /navi prt_mk 158/142 Nearest/random/numbered spots, import instructions and return to Main Office Spot Picker /navi prt_mk 166/142 Choose the closest free spot, a random one or a spot number Market Kafra /navi prt_mk 162/138 Open personal storage

The server generates 4,264 walkable vending spots on a four-cell grid and keeps the central crossing lanes clear. Preparing a shop in Market Street selects the nearest available spot if you are not already on one. Nearby occupied spots are rejected.

Use @vendorspot for the closest free spot, @vendorspot random for a random one, or @vendorspot NUMBER to choose a numbered spot. Your chosen number and the total are displayed after selection. These commands work inside Market Street.

@market returns you to the market center from within Market Street only. Enter from Prontera through Merchants Warp; use the Vending Helper to return to Main Office at 121,22.

Characters without an open shop are returned to Prontera after five minutes. Skills cannot be used while a selling or buying store is open. Market Street is a town with branch use and death penalties disabled.

docs.title: Where shops are allowed
docs.text:
Selling and buying stores may open only on:

Area Map Market Street prt_mk Payon payon Morocc morocc Alberta alberta Comodo comodo

Dungeons and other maps are excluded. Ordinary restricted-cell and trade rules still apply within an allowed map.

docs.title: Find a selling or buying shop
docs.text:
Command Results Price order @ws ITEM / @whosell ITEM Selling shops in the search window Cheapest first @wb ITEM / @whobuy ITEM Buying shops in the search window Highest offer first @ws2 ITEM / @whosell2 ITEM Selling-shop information in chat Cheapest first @wb2 ITEM / @whobuy2 ITEM Buying-shop information in chat Highest offer first

Both the short and long command names are available to ordinary players, including new accounts. They use the same search behavior and filters.

Use an item ID or part of its name. Text results include the item, refine level, quantity, price, shop owner, shop name and navigation coordinates. The text commands do not open a search window.

docs.title: Filters and examples
docs.text:
@ws 504
@ws white potion
@ws +4 2302 0-500000
@wb red potion 45-60
@ws2 gold
@wb2 969

The third example finds Cotton Shirt [1] at +4 or higher, costing up to 500,000z. The fourth finds Red Potion buying offers between 45z and 60z. Enter +REFINE before the item and MIN-MAX after it. Opening @ws or @wb without an item opens the ordinary search interface.

The long names accept the same arguments:

@whosell +7 knife 1000-2000
@whosell2 white potion
@whobuy red herb 65-90
@whobuy2 909

Use @wb or @whobuy for buying offers; @ws and @whosell search selling shops.

docs.title: Remote trading and result limits
docs.text:
Remote purchases and sales through search results are available only in towns, including Market Street. Outside towns, use the text results and navigation to reach a shop. Normal stock, Zeny, capacity, item and trade checks still apply.

Allow two seconds between command searches. Window results are bounded to 200 matches, displayed ten per page; text results show up to 50. Narrow the item name, price range or refine filter when there are more matches. Searches with no matches clear previous result rows.

The existing #trade channel is also available for player advertisements and requests.

docs.title: Open a buying store
docs.text:
Any class can open a buying store with the appropriate license. You must already possess the requested item, have enough Zeny and carrying capacity, and use an allowed shop location. Equipment and crafted/brewed item instances are excluded; tradeable consumables and permitted Etc-tab categories are supported.

Character / service NPC Requirements and price Non-Merchant license Black Marketeer, /navi morocc 45/108 500z per license; up to 100 per purchase Merchant skill unlock Purchasing Team, /navi alberta_in 58/52 Vending Level 1; 10,000z registration; grants Open Buying Store and five starter licenses Merchant replacement licenses Same Purchasing Team 200z per license; up to 100 per purchase

The Purchasing Team is inside the Merchant Guild, reached from Alberta near 35,42.

A license is consumed only when the buying store successfully opens. Canceling setup does not use one. Restoring an already-open offline buying store does not charge a second license; importing a closed shop normally requires a license again.

docs.title: Price limits
docs.text:
Prices are checked when a shop opens, including restored and imported shops.

Shop / item Rule Ordinary item sold by a standard Zeny NPC A vending price above the lowest available NPC catalogue price is lowered to that price Refined, carded, named, random-option or individually serialized item Exempt from the ordinary vending price cap Buying-store offer An offer below the item's NPC resale value is raised to that value

You receive a message for each adjusted price. The vending cap uses the actual loaded catalogues, including our customized dealers, rather than assuming every shop uses the base item-database Buy price.

The existing 2% vending tax remains. Transactions that would exceed a seller's Zeny limit are refused rather than discarding the excess.

docs.title: One listing per stackable item
docs.text:
Each stackable item ID may appear only once across an account's active selling and buying shops, including offline shops. Another character on the account cannot create a second listing for that ID. The same stackable item cannot be repeated in one shop either.

This is an account-based restriction. Hardware-ID enforcement is not enabled, and IP addresses are not used as a substitute.

docs.title: Autotrade 2: keep playing on the same account
docs.text:
1. Open a selling or buying shop in an allowed location, with its items and prices listed.
  2. Type @at2 or @autotrade2.
  3. You should return directly to character selection while the shop stays open.
  4. Choose another character on the same account and continue playing.

Characters vending through @at2 show a [V] marker in character selection and count as offline. Multiple characters on an account can keep shops open, subject to the one-listing-per-item rule.

To close a vendor, log into that character. Its shop closes and its latest saved items and Zeny are loaded before you enter the map. Other vendors on the account stay open. Offline selling and buying shops are saved for restoration after a normal server restart.

The existing @autotrade / @at command remains available. Use @at2 for the explicit return-to-character-selection workflow.

Expected behavior

A successful @at2 should not require a disconnect, a login retry or a second attempt. Chat and commands should work immediately after selecting a character marked [V].

docs.title: Import the last shop
docs.text:
Use @importshop to reopen the most recent shop saved for the current character. It restores the shop name, remaining item listings and prices without entering them all again.

  • History belongs to the character, not the entire account.
  • Items that were sold, moved or no longer match the saved item are omitted.
  • Import does not create replacement stock.
  • Current map, skills/cart, license, Zeny, capacity, pricing and duplicate-listing rules are checked again.
  • Close an existing shop or dialog before importing.

docs.title: Sales recap
docs.text:
Closing a vending shop displays the quantities sold, actual Zeny credited after tax and remaining cart contents. @vendrecap shows the retained sales quantities and Zeny earned for the character's most recent vending shop. The sales recap is retained for an @at2 shop across restoration.

The current recap is a totals summary. A View All menu with individual buyers, sale timestamps and shop opening/closing times is not implemented.

docs.title: November 10 search aliases
docs.text: Added @whosell, @whosell2, @whobuy and @whobuy2 as the long forms of @ws, @ws2, @wb and @wb2. Existing cooldowns and town-only remote trading still apply.

docs.title: Shop and search corrections
docs.text:
• Corrected search-result handling so @ws and @wb safely display the first and subsequent pages. Empty searches clear old rows, the Next option reflects remaining results, and requests past the final page do not return invalid rows.
  • Corrected the disconnect that could occur when issuing commands immediately after logging into a [V] character. The marker is recognized for that character without changing its actual name.
  • Successful @at2 no longer reports a command-failure message.

docs.title: Not enabled
docs.text: Hardware-ID enforcement and a website merchant-search page are deferred. Use the in-game search commands for the current implementation.

docs.title: 🪙 Vestige Coin System
docs.text: Vestige Coins are a tradable currency dropped by eligible monsters. Spend them at Lydia's Coin Exchange, or trade them with other players.

docs.title: The currency
docs.text:
Property Value Item Vestige Coin Item ID 35363 Weight 0 NPC sale value 0z Binding Unbound; not tied to a character or account

Coins can be traded, vended, dropped, placed in carts or personal/guild storage, and mailed, subject to the usual system and map rules.

docs.title: Monster drops
docs.text:
Each eligible monster death has one independent chance to drop one coin.

Monster Chance Eligible monsters without an exception below 5% Familiar, Female Thief Bug, Male Thief Bug and Orc Zombie 1%

The same reduced or excluded rule applies to database variants of those species.

docs.title: Monsters that do not drop coins
docs.text:
• Hydra
  • Thief Bug Egg, Peco Peco Egg and Ant Egg
  • Blue, Green, Yellow, White and Shining Plants
  • Black and Red Mushrooms
  • Thief Bug, Tarou and Plankton

The roll requires normal player loot credit. Special player-summon AI, clones, guardians, no-loot deaths and expired summons do not generate coins.

docs.title: Fixed chances
docs.text:
Coin chances stay at 5% or 1%. Weekday/weekend rates, boss-drop rates, Bubble Gum, LUK and other drop modifiers do not increase them.

Normal loot ownership, party sharing, pickup rules and carrying limits still apply. You can add #35363 to an Autoloot group or ignore list. Percentage filtering uses the coin's original 5% or 1% chance; an active group's explicit item choice takes priority over the ignore list.

docs.title: Where to spend them
docs.text:
Visit Lydia at prt_in 38,108: /navi prt_in 38/108. Enter the Coin Exchange building through Prontera 133,183. Her shop accepts Vestige Coins and offers consumables, supply boxes and reusable wings. See the complete exchange catalogue.

Astrid at Prontera 147,187 also accepts Vestige Coins together with crafting ingredients for 22 headgear quests. Her guide lists every reward, material quantity and effect.

Vestige Coins are separate from hourly Gold Coins and Card Exchange points. Existing quests and events do not award Vestige Coins unless that reward is explicitly added later.

docs.title: 💤 Visual AFK Status
docs.text:
Characters show an AFK sign above their head after 60 seconds of inactivity on eligible hunting maps. The sign temporarily replaces the upper-headgear appearance. Your equipped item and its bonuses stay unchanged.

Walking, attacking, using a skill or using an item clears the sign immediately and restores your equipped appearance. Equipping an item also counts as activity.

docs.title: Where it appears
docs.text:
The indicator applies outside towns and town interiors. It is suppressed while vending, running a buying shop or using autotrade, and on WoE castle maps.

The feature is automatic. It does not change your Autoloot configuration.

docs.title: 🌍 Warper
docs.text:
Updated: November 22, 2026.

Travel to 34 towns and Misty Island through the Warper. Find her at Prontera 159,187, marked with a Warper bubble:

/navi prontera 159/187

docs.title: How to travel
docs.text:
1. Speak to the Warper and choose Midgard Towns, New World, Islands or Misty Island.
  2. Read the fee beside the destination name.
  3. Select the town to pay and warp immediately. There is no separate Pay and Travel confirmation.

Choose Back or Cancel to leave without paying. The NPC checks access, destination availability and your Zeny before charging. Insufficient Zeny or an unavailable destination does not charge you; a failed transfer to the destination map returns the travel fee.

docs.title: Travel fees
docs.text:
Category Fee per trip Nearby Midgard towns 2,000z Distant Midgard towns 3,600z New World 25,000z Islands 20,000z Misty Island 5,000z, after your first voyage with Captain Janssen

Midgard's nearby/distant groups are based on proximity to Prontera. Each destination has a fixed fee.

docs.title: Nearby towns - 2,000z
docs.text: Prontera, Izlude, Geffen, Payon, Alberta, Morroc.

docs.title: Distant towns - 3,600z
docs.text:
Aldebaran, Comodo, Umbala, Niflheim, Lutie, Jawaii, Yuno, Hugel, Einbroch, Einbech, Lighthalzen, Rachel, Veins.

Jawaii is available through this Warper without marriage or quest requirements. Its travel fee is 3,600z.

docs.title: New World
docs.text:
Every destination below costs 25,000z and requires completion of Onward to the New World.

Destination Additional access requirement Midgard Expedition Camp None beyond New World access Splendide None beyond New World access Manuk None beyond New World access Mora None beyond New World access El Dicastes Complete El Dicastes visitor registration with Clerk Rhawyne Eclage Complete Eclage immigration with the Security Guard

docs.title: Unlocking destinations
docs.text:
Access belongs to each character. Quest-locked towns are hidden from the travel list until that character completes the required entrance quest. They appear automatically the next time you open the menu, including for characters who completed the quest previously.

Choose Access requirements in the main menu to see what is still missing. Visiting the map or holding a quest item does not substitute for finishing the quest. Access is checked again before the travel fee is deducted.

For El Dicastes, finish the visitor registration rather than stopping at the invitation. For Eclage, finish the immigration process with the Security Guard. Both also require New World access.

docs.title: Islands
docs.text:
The former Foreign Lands categories are combined into Islands. All nine destinations cost 20,000z:

  • Amatsu
  • Ayothaya
  • Gonryun
  • Louyang
  • Moscovia
  • Brasilis
  • Dewata
  • Malangdo
  • Port Malaya

The towns listed here do not require a separate entrance quest through this Warper. Quests that unlock a town's dungeon still apply to that dungeon.

docs.title: Misty Island
docs.text:
The Misty Island - 5,000z category takes you to the staging area for Endless Tower and Endless Cellar. Complete your first voyage through Captain Janssen at Prontera 217,187 to unlock this route for that character.

The destination costs 5,000z per trip and appears after the unlock. The tower's level, party and weekly admission requirements still apply separately.
